query: European Commission DMA non-compliance decision against Google Search Article 6(5) self-preferencing July 2026 - has a formal decision been adopted or announced? Latest status as of mid-July 2026
answer:
## Summary

**As of mid-July 2026 (July 17), the European Commission had NOT yet formally adopted or announced the record DMA non-compliance fine decision against Google for Article 6(5) self-preferencing in Search — but it was imminent.**

Key findings:

- **July 15, 2026:** The *Financial Times* reported the Commission would adopt a **series of DMA decisions "next week"** (week of July 20–24), including the Search self-preferencing fine plus a Google Play fine.
- **July 16, 2026:** The Commission issued **binding remedy/specification orders** (Android AI access for rivals; Search data-sharing) — but these carried **no fine** and are legally distinct from the Article 6(5) non-compliance fine decision.
- **Expected fine:** "High triple-digit million euros" (~€700M–€1B) — would be the **largest DMA fine to date**, exceeding Apple's ~€500M and Meta's ~€200M.

**Critical distinction to note for forecasting:** Headlines around July 16 conflated two things — (1) the *remedy orders* (issued, no fine) and (2) the *Article 6(5) non-compliance fine decision* (still pending/expected imminently, not confirmed adopted). The fine decision (case DMA.100193) traces back to proceedings opened March 25, 2024 and preliminary findings in March 2025, and had been repeatedly delayed amid US-EU trade sensitivities. All fine reporting was sourced from unnamed insiders (FT, Handelsblatt); no official EC press release confirming the fine had been published at the snapshot date.

Full structured findings with sources and data points have been submitted.

key_facts: As of mid-July 2026 (July 17), the formal Article 6(5) self-preferencing non-compliance fine decision against Google had NOT been officially adopted/announced by the European Commission — it was reported as imminent.

Financial Times reported July 15, 2026 that the Commission would adopt a series of DMA decisions against Google 'next week' (week of July 20–24, 2026), including the Search self-preferencing fine and a Google Play fine.
The expected fine is in the 'high triple-digit million euro' range (~€700M–€1B), which would be the largest DMA fine to date, exceeding Apple's ~€500M and Meta's ~€200M DMA fines.

On July 16, 2026 the Commission issued BINDING remedy/specification orders (Android AI access for rivals; Search data-sharing with competitors) — these carried NO fine and are distinct from the Article 6(5) non-compliance fine decision.
The Article 6(5) case (DMA.100193, Alphabet – Online Search Engine) stems from non-compliance proceedings opened March 25, 2024 and preliminary findings issued in March 2025.
The decision had been repeatedly delayed for months, reportedly amid geopolitical/US-EU trade sensitivities.
Search data-sharing obligations reported to begin ~January 2027; Android AI access obligations ~July 2027; Commission to conclude related proceedings within ~six months of July 16, 2026.
On March 15, 2026, 18 industry/consumer groups sent an open letter urging a formal non-compliance decision before the two-year mark (March 25, 2026).
The fine is below the DMA maximum (10% of Alphabet's global turnover, ~€35B), reportedly reflecting Google concessions.
All fine reporting was sourced from unnamed insiders (FT, Handelsblatt); no official EC press release confirming the fine decision had been published as of mid-July 2026.
